title: Experts on “voter fraud” in Sweden: Nothing indicates that it is happening deliberately
content:
In recent weeks, claims of electoral fraud have appeared on social media. But what has happened, and does everything being highlighted really constitute electoral fraud? NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån examine a few examples with political scientists.

“It’s voter fraud,” says Malmölistan party leader Nils Littorin as he walks around looking for his party’s ballot papers at a polling station. The video, posted on X two weeks ago, has been viewed nearly 350,000 times.

Video on X on 26 August.

“It’s probably some private individual who took the ballot papers,” one person says in the comments.

Nils Littorin replies: “Damn it, that’s electoral fraud just the same. It doesn’t matter WHO does it. Keep fighting to defend the fraud.”

Since early voting began this year, there have been several claims of electoral fraud on social media. Among other things, several small parties have posted videos in which election officials are accused of failing to put out ballot papers for all parties in the screened-off areas. Others have reported being turned away when they tried to vote while wearing clothing displaying political propaganda.

title: Rumours of voter fraud spread after voting problems in Sweden
content:
“Voter fraud everywhere,” a person wrote on X about advance votes that were incorrectly registered. But the Swedish Election Authority rejects the claim, NORDIS partner Källkritikbyrån reports.

Last Friday the Swedish Election Authority reported a technical error that was then feared to affect approximately 4,000 advance votes. Over the weekend, the error concerning advance votes was analysed, and it was found that at most 500 advance votes are affected.

The figure may decrease further, the Swedish Election Authority writes on its website, and regrets that it will probably not be possible to determine who cast these votes.

– The error occurred because election officials began accepting a new vote before they had completed the voting process for the previous voter. As a result, the votes were registered incorrectly, Jenny Stad, press officer at the Swedish Election Authority, told Källkritikbyrån.

Post on X on 4 September.
